page: Microsoft Azure M416-208s_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MSv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by Intel Xeon 8280L processors, delivering 208 dedicated vCPUs across 104 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz and includes a 38 MB L3 cache. This server is equipped with an exceptionally large memory capacity of 5700.0 GB, providing approximately 27.4 GB per core, and includes 8389 GB of local storage with support for Premium Storage. No GPUs are bundled with this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression, fall into the lower tier. However, the massive core count enables top-tier multi-core performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores. Memory subsystem performance is highly efficient, with top-tier memory bandwidth reaching 10446.46 GB/sec for cached read-only small blocks and 651.24 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Redis SET operations also perform exceptionally well, achieving 162.62 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a high-density hardware profile designed for specialized enterprise workloads. The massive memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial local storage capacity make it highly suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, heavy multi-threaded data processing, and enterprise resource planning systems. Conversely, it is poorly suited for workloads reliant on high single-threaded performance or GPU acceleration.
